newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 13.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) share price has been falling for the past 4 months, and could be at levels low enough to tempt fresh buyers, technical analysts say. If the stock can rally above A$15.90, then the buyers are seen re-surfacing. Copper prices, however, fell again overnight.

reported a 22 percent slide in first-half 1996 earnings on Thursday, blaming lower industrial metal prices and other operational difficulties for the losses. But the group remained upbeat for metals demand and prices over the rest of this year and into 1997. "It's disappointing for us to have to report a drop in earnings," said Robert Wilson, chief executive of the group which merged in December last year. "But in the longer term we are very optimistic about the future demand prospects (for metals)," he added. RTZ leapt 31p to 961-1/2, boosted by comments from the mining group that it saw signs of rising metal prices.

Australis Media Ltd plans to announce later on Friday a modified equity funding package injecting more than the US$105 million originally announced in August, a source close to the company said. Australis would also announce it had secured the approval from U.S. bondholders needed for a new bond issue of between US$150 million to US$170 million by October this year, the source said.
Sydney-based seafood retailer Manettas Ltd, controlled by South Africa's Bidvest Group, said on Friday it plans a two-for-three rights issue at 47 cents a share to raise up to A$29.7 million.

Australian clothing retailer Country Road Ltd said on Friday it had agreed to sell 25 percent of its U.S. operations to Japanese trading house Itochu Corp and that Itochu would market Country Road products in Japan.
